AM7-01.note: Option set is the 2x2 grid {12,6} x {+,-}. Legitimate ACT convention, but see template group 1: this is the same 'isolate the named variable' habit as AM7-11 and AM7-19.

AM7-02.note: Options are {<,>} x {-4,4}; the sign-flip trap is the whole item.

AM7-03.solved: 12 cm / 2 cm = 6 map units; 6 x 3 km = 18 km.
AM7-03.note: 8 = inverted ratio (12 x 2/3), 24 = 12 x 2. 15 is the weakest option - hard to name the wrong path that produces it.

AM7-04.note: 2x2 grid: {12,7} (multiply vs add coefficients) x {x^12y^2, x^7y^3} (multiply vs add exponents).

AM7-05.note: Options are {2, 1/2} x {+,-}: reciprocal error and sign error, both real.

AM7-06.note: 36 and 9 are both intermediate values a student stops at; 17 is 14+5-... (adds instead of subtracts). Good.

AM7-09.note: 16 = (12+20)/2, the intended trap, and it is a good one. Still medium, not hard: harmonic-mean average speed is a single learned habit, not two ideas interacting.

AM7-10.note: x != 3 is correctly excluded in the stem. Factoring both pieces is two recognitions but they do not interact - it is sequential, so medium.

AM7-11.note: Template group 1 with AM7-01 and AM7-19: same habit, same 2x2 option grid ({2A/h, A/h} x {+,-}). A student who learns this once answers all three.

AM7-12.note: STEM DEFECT (not fatal): (-13)(-11) = 143 too, and the smaller of those is -13. The stem should say 'two consecutive positive odd integers'. -13 is not an option so exclusivity holds, but a careful student is briefly stuck. 12 and 14 read as consecutive-EVEN confusion.

AM7-13.note: 32 (the ratio itself) and 20 (four doublings) are both real wrong paths.

AM7-14.note: 2x2 grid {6,8} x {x^9,x^4}: 6 = 4 x 3/2, x^4 = 6 x 2/3. Template group 3 with AM7-04 and AM7-23.

AM7-15.note: NEAR-DUPLICATE of AM7-21 - identical move ((sum)^2 - 2(product)) in different clothes. 81 (forgot the subtraction) and 95 (subtracted xy once) are good. One of these two items should be replaced.

AM7-16.solved: Multiply numerator and denominator by 3x: (3 + x)/(3 - x) = (x+3)/(3-x).
AM7-16.note: Sign-of-denominator trap is well built: C is the same expression with the denominator negated.

AM7-17.note: 20 = the length (answered the wrong quantity), which is the intended trap. 13 and 16 are thinner. Template group 2 with AM7-18 and AM7-20.

AM7-18.note: 7 = the pens (wrong quantity). Same structure and same trap as AM7-17 and AM7-20.

AM7-19.note: This is AM7-11 with a square root added: same isolate-the-variable habit, same {2s/a, s/(2a)} x {root, no root} grid. Stem does not state t > 0, but the physical reading forces it; not a real ambiguity.

AM7-20.note: 23 = the larger number, 18 = half the sum. Third member of template group 2.

AM7-21.note: Same identity as AM7-15. 25 (forgot the 2) and 27 (added instead of subtracted) are both genuine.

AM7-22.note: Genuinely hard: the absolute-value bound and the parity count interact - the fractional lower endpoint (-5.67) and whether 0 counts both decide the answer. 15 = every integer in range, 4 = positive evens only. Best-built item in the batch.

AM7-23.note: Rewriting to a common base is one habit and the rest is a five-line linear solve - medium, not hard. 4 and 7 are thin.

AM7-24.solved: Infinitely many means the equations are proportional: 6/3 = 2, so k = 10/2 = 5 and c = 2 x 12 = 24. k + c = 29.
AM7-24.note: One recognition (proportional coefficients) applied twice, not two ideas interacting. Authored-hard items like this are why the band inflates. 17 = 5 + 12, 11 = 5 + 6 are real slips.

AM7-25.solved: (x+3 + x-3)/((x-3)(x+3)) = 1 -> 2x = x^2 - 9 -> x^2 - 2x - 9 = 0. Product of roots = -9 (discriminant 40 > 0, neither root is +-3).
AM7-25.note: Hard and correctly so: the quadratic does not factor, so the student must either use Vieta or multiply two irrational roots. 2 = the SUM of the roots, which is the exact right trap. Second of only four real hard items.

AM7-26.note: AUTHORED HARD, GRADED MEDIUM - the closest call in the batch. The 'at least' adds no second idea: it is solved exactly like an equation and the answer is the boundary. Mixture setup is one learned template. 72 = the resulting total volume, which is the one strong option.

AM7-27.solved: Roots multiply to 36 and differ by 5: factor pairs (1,36),(2,18),(3,12),(4,9),(6,6) -> (4,9). k = sum = 13.
AM7-27.note: Two constraints (Vieta product and the difference) have to be satisfied together, then converted to the sum - that is real interaction. 37 and 20 are the sums of the (1,36) and (2,18) pairs, i.e. exactly what you get by dropping the difference condition; 9 is the larger root. Distractors are the best-derived set here.

AM7-28.note: Hard: the nth-term formula and the sum formula must be used simultaneously as a system - neither alone gets there. 27.5 = 165/6 (the mean), 23 = the 3rd term, 9 = the common difference. Every option is a real stopping point.
